newsitem.title: JAPAN: KDD says seeks tie-ups with multiple carriers.
newsitem.headline: KDD says seeks tie-ups with multiple carriers.

text.p: Japanese international telecommunications company Kokusai Denshin Denwa Co Ltd (KDD) said on Monday it is seeking business tie-ups with several long-distance carriers in the domestic market, denying speculation that it is merging with DDI Corp.
"We are in talks with Teleway Japan and telecom units of electric power utilities on forming business tie-ups such as the one with DDI," a KDD spokeswoman said.
"We are not considering a merger with DDI for the time being," she added.
KDD and DDI announced earlier on Monday that they would start offering seamless phone services combining their long-distance and international services in October under a unified brand.
The rates for the new service, to be offered through a Japanese unit of KDD, will be about 20 percent lower than those of their competitors, a KDD spokeswoman said.
KDD, the formerly government-owned carrier specialising in international services, was allowed to offer domestic services in June.
Teleway Japan Corp, a domestic long-distance operator, is an affiliate of Toyota Motor Corp.

Last year KDD said it was considering forming business partnerships with telecom affiliates of electric power utilities, which are offering long-distance services to a small group of corporate users using fibre-optic networks.
